bug_title: An exception thrown by delay function, when Time object not initialized
bug_description:
The tf2_ros is a C++ package that is using the ros::Time object to sleep (a C++ object).  This object might not be initialized if running inside rospy (so from python API to ros).  In such case an exception is thrown and sleeping fails.
The fix of the bug catches the exception and uses the wall clock time API to delay instead.
The problem and the fix are ROS-specific.  However the issue of using uninitialized APIs due to configuration issues is a fairly general one.
The PR is rather uninformative.  The best explanation can be found in the first link in the 'links' section.

bug_title: Potential Race Condition on Serial Writes
bug_description: The Kobuki driver communicates with the actual robot by sending commands over a serial cable. This interface was not protected against concurrent accesses, while being used in an environment that, more often that not, features multithreading.

The "MAVConnTCPServer::client_closed" method is responsible for safely closing a given client's connection to the TCP server. In the buggy implementation of this method, the lock for the client (represented as a pointer to an MAVConnTCPClient instance) was not acquired before closing the connection, leading to a possible race condition that can result in deadlocking or a segmentation fault.

bug_title: New features unavailable in older systems
bug_description: When adding the possibility to use features that have been added in new versions of Robot Web Services (RWS), then it will not be possible to use them with older systems. Currently, if using an older system version, then this will be attempted and reported as a failed communication. It might be prudent to check the current system's version and then report if a specific function is unavailable.

bug_title: Wrong Inertia and Center of Mass in Robot Description
bug_description: The URDF file for Kobuki's physical model assumed the center of mass to be in the center of the robot's cylinder body. This is wrong, since the battery was intentionally placed at the front of the robot to make it heavier at the front. The wrong placement of the robot's center of mass had the effect of having it constantly bouncing back and forth in the Gazebo simulator.

bug_title: Incorrect parameter names used to fetch values
bug_description: Lines 311--313 are used to fetch the current x, y, and z coordinates. The "ros::NodeHandle::param" function used to fetch these values accepts the name of a parameter, a reference to the variable to which its value should be written, and a default value which should be written to the variable in the case that no parameter can be found that matches the given name. Lines 312 and 313 incorrectly retrieve the "sensor_position/x" value for all three dimensions of the position of the sensor (ie: x, y and z), rather than the correct "sensor_position/y" and "sensor_position/z" parameters.
